panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Morning rush in Neo-Vectra. Commuters, bags, coffee, transit noise. One woman stops dead when she sees a man she does not know. Keep the event small inside an ordinary crowd.
Panel 2 — Woman: 'I know you.' Man: 'We've never met.' Their bodies disagree with their words: she is frightened by recognition; he is frightened by her certainty.
Panel 3 — Woman: 'You left me at the south gate.' Man: 'What south gate?' Let nearby strangers begin noticing, but do not turn the plaza into riot spectacle.
Panel 4 — Theo, Rae and Adrian enter the edge of the scene. Rae reaches the woman first and says, 'Don't tell her she's wrong.'

Panel 5 — Theo turns from the distressed woman toward Rae: 'What do we tell her?' Rae keeps one hand lightly on the woman's forearm and answers, 'That she's here now.' The stranger she remembers remains several feet away, unsure whether to approach.

Panel 6 — End on the woman still looking at the stranger with grief for a relationship neither present biography can explain. The public crisis begins as two people unable to reconcile what they feel.

Panel 1 — Ancient Neo-Vectra command balcony above a populated city already preparing for war. Oryon looks out at people he has seen die in possible futures; Arbiter watches him rather than the tactical display.
Panel 2 — Oryon: 'If we wait, this city becomes the beginning.' Arbiter: 'Of what?' Keep Oryon's certainty burdened rather than grandiose.
Panel 3 — Oryon: 'Everything we have been trying to prevent.' Show fear on him before Arbiter challenges the claim.
Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'You've said that before.' Oryon: 'Because it keeps being true.' Their history with this argument should be visible.
Panel 5 — Arbiter: 'Or because you keep looking for the same ending.' End on Oryon absorbing the possibility that foresight itself may have habits.

Panel 1 — Side street off the transit plaza. Small groups have formed around hand-drawn versions of symbols people remember without context. Phones and ordinary conversation spread stories faster than any ancient technology.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'They deserve to know what those marks mean.' He watches someone clutch a symbol with unexplained loyalty.
Panel 3 — Rae: 'They deserve not to get killed while we're explaining it.' Show two strangers beginning to accuse each other based on recovered feeling rather than facts.

Panel 4 — Theo: 'So we lie again?' Rae pivots sharply toward him, one hand still extended between two strangers who have begun arguing over the recovered symbols. Her jaw tightens; Theo stops mid-step.

Panel 5 — Rae: 'No. We keep them from choosing a war before they remember why it ended.' End on the symbols held by ordinary people whose present relationships matter as much as the recovered loyalties.

Panel 1 — Ancient residential concourse under evacuation. Atlas physically shields civilians while Oryon arrives with Mero, urging withdrawal. Put named-looking, specific people around them rather than anonymous crowd texture.
Panel 2 — Oryon: 'You are saving the people who can see you.' Atlas: 'They're still people.' Atlas remains actively helping someone while answering.
Panel 3 — Oryon: 'So are the ones who die if this gets out.' His grief points beyond the frame; do not make him cold.
Panel 4 — Atlas: 'Then help me save both.' Oryon: 'There is no both.' Let the impossibility land between them as a genuine wound.
Panel 5 — Mero watches a child or injured civilian pass between the two champions, seeing the cost of turning lives into sides of an argument.
Panel 6 — Mero: 'That false choice keeps ruining us.' End with neither champion able to dismiss the other, because both are looking at real people they believe they are protecting.

Panel 1 — Return to the same physical concourse in the present. The architecture is ordinary modern life over an old footprint; Theo recognizes where Atlas once stood, but the couple in front of him is more important.
Panel 2 — The man recoils from the woman he loves: 'You were with them.' She answers, 'With who?' Keep their present intimacy visible in clothes, touch, shared belongings or familiarity.
Panel 3 — Man: 'I don't know.' His fear is real even though he cannot name its source.

Panel 4 — The woman steps directly in front of the man, close enough that their shared bag and interlocked key ring remain visible between them: 'Then look at me.' He forces his eyes from the recovered symbol back to her face.
Panel 5 — Adrian, quietly: 'This is what I was afraid of.' He sees the exact social fracture that once justified the Reset to him.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'Fear isn't a plan.' End tight on the couple still facing each other, hands close but not touching, while Adrian and the city recede soft in the background.

directionInline.text: Keep Flux's established place visibly empty at the table: unused chair and the same abandoned cup or papers from earlier scenes. Frame each speaker with that empty place somewhere in the composition at least once.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient command hall. Starbreaker, Redlin, Oryon and Mero occupy a tense table; one familiar place remains conspicuously empty, with no explanation attached to it.
Panel 2 — Oryon: 'We know where this ends.' Redlin: 'No. Flux knew enough to stop saying that.' His eyes move to the empty place.
Panel 3 — Starbreaker: 'Flux left.' Redlin: 'Maybe because none of you listened.' Redlin points once toward Flux's empty chair; Starbreaker looks there instead of back at Redlin.
Panel 4 — Oryon: 'Or because looking became unbearable.' Keep Oryon seated nearest the empty place, eyes on the abandoned cup or papers, shoulders lowered before he looks back to the others.
Panel 5 — Mero: 'Either way, Flux isn't here to choose for us.' End with the empty place still unresolved. Responsibility remains in the room while certainty has left it.

directionInline.text: Municipal shelter with cots, blankets, first-aid supplies and volunteers physically separating two arguing people while keeping families together. Rae steps between the conflict, then kneels to help one person; Theo and Adrian continue talking while doing useful work.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Municipal shelter after several fights. Volunteers separate people, tend minor injuries and keep families together. Theo, Rae and Adrian argue while doing useful work rather than standing over a map.
Panel 2 — Adrian: 'Move them away from the old sites.' Theo hears the old reflex immediately: 'There it is.'
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I'm trying to stop people from hurting each other.' Theo: 'By taking the memory away again.' Keep Adrian morally serious, not authoritarian for convenience.
Panel 4 — A fresh argument breaks out nearby. Rae physically steps between two people before turning back to Theo and Adrian.

Panel 5 — Rae: 'Stop. Both of you. We contain violence. Not memory.' She immediately turns away from Theo and Adrian, kneels beside one of the people she separated and presses a clean cloth to a cut while volunteers steady the other person nearby.
Panel 1 — Ancient Mero staff room during Neo-Vectra. Senior voices argue muffled beyond a door; Mero has pulled junior Theo aside because the official arguments have stopped producing thought.
Panel 2 — Mero: 'Everyone has an answer.' Theo: 'That's the problem.' Mero's tired amusement shows why he keeps asking Theo.
Panel 3 — Mero jokes about promoting him for insulting command staff. Theo does not take the bait; he says, 'Put them in one room.'
Panel 4 — Mero: 'They are in one room.' Theo: 'No. Their arguments are.' Let Theo point toward the closed room full of factions reduced to positions.
Panel 5 — Theo: 'Put the people there.' Mero looks through the half-open door toward the senior council room, then back at Theo. He reaches for the door handle but pauses before opening it.

Panel 1 — Neo-Vectra plaza at night. Handmade signs carry recovered faction symbols beside present-day names, family photos and hastily written personal stories. Organization grows through people talking to one another.
Panel 2 — Theo sees strangers sorting themselves into groups and says, 'I thought remembering would make it make sense.'
Panel 3 — Rae: 'Memory doesn't make anyone better.' Behind her, two people with the same recovered symbol disagree sharply, preventing a simplistic faction split.

Panel 4 — Theo stands in the plaza and watches two opposite reactions at once: one pair of strangers embraces after recognition while another person steps backward from someone reaching toward them. Keep both pairs visible behind Theo in the same wide frame.
Panel 5 — Rae: 'Ask Adrian. He tried the alternative.'
Panel 6 — End on the plaza as a mixture of reunion, argument, fear and curiosity. Truth has produced agency, not harmony.
Panel 1 — Ancient Arbiter workroom. Rae sits beside Arbiter with physical lists of neighborhoods and names, not abstract casualty graphics.
Panel 2 — Arbiter: 'I need the remaining sectors.' Rae corrects him: 'You mean the people we haven't reached.'
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'I mean both.' Rae: 'Then say both.' Rae taps the physical list of neighborhood names with the end of her pen; Arbiter looks down at the same page before answering.
Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'Fine. Who do we reach first?' Rae studies the names and chooses: 'The south gate. Then the river housing.'
Panel 5 — Arbiter asks, 'And the north?' Hold on Rae because she understands exactly what her ordering means.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'I know.' End with the unchosen names still physically present. Humanizing the language did not remove the consequence of choosing.
Panel 1 — Quiet rooftop above the arguing city. Theo and Rae sit without Adrian. The noise below is distant enough that they finally have to consider their own remembered participation.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'I pushed Mero toward the council.' Rae: 'I chose who got out first.' Neither minimizes the other's admission.
Panel 3 — Theo: 'We didn't start the war.' Rae: 'No.' Give the answer no comforting emphasis.
Panel 4 — Theo: 'That doesn't feel as helpful as I wanted.' A trace of the person he used to be is recognizable in the admission.
Panel 5 — Rae: 'It shouldn't.' End on them sharing responsibility without collapsing themselves into ancient guilt or declaring their present lives false.
Panel 1 — Overlook before dawn. Below, ordinary people continue arguing, reuniting, writing down memories and trying to sleep. Adrian joins Theo and Rae.
Panel 2 — Adrian: 'You keep asking what happens if everyone remembers.' Theo answers, 'Yes.'
Panel 3 — Adrian gives the first example: someone remembers a wife they never married. Show one ordinary pair below, but do not literalize every example as prophecy.

Panel 4 — Adrian continues: someone remembers killing the man who is now their brother; a city remembers belonging to an enemy that no longer exists. Keep his focus on relationships and identities, not institutions.

Panel 5 — Rae: 'And you thought forgetting was kinder.' Adrian: 'I thought it was the only thing we hadn't tried.' End on Adrian leaning against the overlook rail, shoulders rounded, while below them scattered people write memories, argue quietly and try to sleep under temporary lights.
